text:
mike-thompson: Hey team — quick Q. I need to be in Spain (Barcelona) for ~10 weeks this summer to help my partner with a family thing. I want to stay on Redwood payroll and keep benefits. Do I need to change my homebase? Will the WFH stipend continue? Any tax/social implications I should expect?

sara-people-ops: Thanks for the heads-up, Mike. Short answer: maybe. Main factors are the duration and whether you’re doing any client-facing work there. 10 weeks is borderline for some countries. We need to treat this as a temporary cross-border remote request.

mike-thompson: OK — what do you need from me to start?

sara-people-ops: Please submit the "Temporary Remote Work (Cross-Border)" form with dates, full address in Spain, manager approval screenshot, and the reason (brief). Also confirm you'll remain on Redwood systems only (no third-party contracting).

anna-payroll: Adding payroll notes: if you stay < 30 days generally no payroll or social security change, but Spain has rules that can trigger registration if you’re physically in-country and working. At ~10 weeks we may need to consult local tax counsel. We’ll triage once we have the form.

mike-thompson: Got it. So is the WFH stipend pro-rated for that period?

sara-people-ops: Stipend: remote/WFH allowance is normally tied to your homebase country. For temporary relocations under 3 months we typically continue the stipend, prorated for the month boundary. If payroll needs to move or employee is on a different legal payroll, stipend handling can change — we’ll confirm after payroll/legal review.

it-support: Re: equipment — we can ship a spare monitor and keyboard to Spain if approved. Please open an IT ticket with shipping address and dates. Note: warranty/returns are local-coverage dependent.

mike-thompson: Any visa/immigration steps I should consider? It’s EU for a US passport — will likely need to check entry length.

sara-people-ops: We’re not immigration lawyers, but practical note: check Schengen 90/180 day rule. If your passport is US, 10 weeks (~70 days) is within the 90-day visa-free limit, but confirm for your exact dates. If you need to do anything beyond tourist activities (e.g., local contracting), stop and talk to legal.

anna-payroll: We’ll run a short risk assessment after the form. Things we look at: 1) tax exposure (permanent establishment unlikely for one employee but depends on activities), 2) social security (totalization), 3) benefits continuity, 4) payroll withholding obligations. Expect a 3–5 business day turnaround for initial assessment.

mike-thompson: Thanks. Is there a template to include manager approval?

sara-people-ops: Yep — paste this into the form or your manager can reply in Slack. Quick template: 

``
Manager Approval: I approve Mike Thompson to work remotely from Barcelona from 2026-06-01 to 2026-08-10. I understand Payroll and People Ops will complete any necessary checks.
Manager: Priya Rao
Date: 2026-05-10
``

sara-people-ops: Also tagging @anna-payroll and @tax-ops-bot to start the prelim check once Mike files the form.

tax-ops-bot: Automated reminder: for temporary cross-border requests >30 days, please attach the full street address + expected work hours (local timezone) to the form.

mike-thompson: Done — I submitted the form and attached my manager approval.

anna-payroll: Received. We’ll triage today. If we need local tax counsel, we’ll notify you and PSL (people-ops) will coordinate any docs you need to sign.

mike-thompson: Appreciate it. One last Q — will I lose my US health coverage while in Spain for that period?

sara-people-ops: Typically you remain covered under US medical while traveling short-term, but international claims vary. We’ll confirm with benefits. If it’s a gap risk, we’ll propose options (temp travel insurance).

mike-thompson: Sounds good. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sara-people-ops: Thanks — closing loop once payroll confirms. If anyone has specific Spain experience or tips (housing, co-working), DM Mike.
